description:
Executor the desktop workflow application for Windows. Speed up your daily workflow, opening things and doing things.

Executor the desktop workflow application for Windows. Speed up your daily workflow, opening things and doing things.

Key Features:
- Launch applications, files, folders, websites, web services (with parameters) and prompts in milliseconds.
- Trigger multiple actions with one text command and/or hotkey.
- Let's be an expert in opening up the world instead of trying to put the whole world inside of Executor (as some alternatives try to do).
- Take the clipboard to a new level, swiftly trigger system commands, do fast calculations, manage running applications and more.
- Tailor keywords, appearance, hotkeys, and behavior to perfectly match your daily workflow.
- Customize the look and feel with various skins and theming options to match your desktop setup.
What's new
- You can now have multiple notes in Executor. You can also use a note as a text snippet to send to other windows, and you can use a note as a text variable within keywords commands and parameters. More details:
  - The Notes window has a new "Notes" button that will open a sidebar with a notes list to manage notes.
  - Right-click the notes list for a context-menu with various options also listing some shortcut hotkeys.
  - Sort alphabetically or by modified.
  - Pin notes in the Notes window.
  - Filter notes in the Notes window.
  - Notes are saved as .txt files in a "notes" sub-folder in the Executor data folder.
  - -n and notes ($NOTES$) also supports adding directly to a specific note by -n [note-name]: [message]. Example -n shopping: milk adds to the "shopping" note, where -n milk adds to the default note.
  - Added the command $NOTEOPEN$ that takes the note name as a parameter. This makes it possible to have a keyword that always open a specific note. Example: Keyword.name=shopping keyword.command=$NOTEOPEN$ keyword.parameters=Shopping
  - Added $N [note-name] this will inject the text of a note in a keyword command or keyword parameters, also added $NU [note-name] that do the same but also URL encode the text of the note.
  - For $SENDTEXT..$ keywords commands that already supported {FILE [filename]} now also supports {NOTE [note-name]} to send the text of a note.
  - In the the multi-line input and in the clipboard list you can save the text as new Note by using the right-click menu.
  - New default keyword nl will list Notes and filter notes if given a parameter. This also has a right-click menu with options like send a note's text to current window etc. You can import this from default.exc (type imports). It's using the keyword command $NOTELIST$.
  - Added input command -an to add a new note directly from Executor's input, without opening the notes window first. It uses the same name: text format as -n, so the two work as a pair: -an creates a note and -n adds to an existing one. -an shopping: milk, eggs creates a new note named "shopping" containing "milk, eggs". The notes window stays closed, so it's just as quick as -n.. -an shopping (no text) creates an empty note named “shopping” and opens it, ready for typing
  - If you have the backup option enabled or trigger the backup manually via a keyword then notes are backed up (zipped) to a folder named "notes-backup" located in Executor's data folder. Also the default notes are still also backed up as notes.txt.bak as well.
  - Added a "Notes, snippets and text variables" section to the Docs page.
- You can now send formatted text (like a fancy email signature) to other windows using $SENDTEXT2$ and $SENDTEXT3$ using the new tag {RICH c:\some folder\signature.html}. This supports .html/.htm and .rtf files and keeps the formatting (bold, colors, links, tables etc.) when pasted into apps that support it, like Google Docs, Gmail, Outlook, Word, Slack and Teams. Apps that only support plain text (like Notepad) will get a plain text version. Tip: HTML is supported by many more apps than RTF, so prefer .html if you can. An easy way to make one is to save an email signature or a webpage snippet as .html. With $SENDTEXT$ (which types the text) the plain text version is typed instead.
- Executor now indexes Windows settings pages, like the Start menu search does. Type for example wifi, bluetooth or night light to open that page in Windows Settings directly. The pages are listed in windowssettings.txt (next to Executor.exe), one per line as name=link. You can rename or translate entries, or add your own (e.g. Device Manager=devmgmt.msc). To keep your changes across updates, put your copy in Executor's data folder (type -folder). Requires Windows 10 or later. Can be turned on/off in Settings > Indexing & cache.
Improvements
- Added a "I prefer larger fonts" option to the wizard.
Fixes
- The apps list could be cut short by the list's maximum number of items and not show all apps.
- Sometimes the mouse cursor could be stuck on a certain cursor type in the Notes window.
- Sometimes when using the -n command the Notes window could move behind Executor.
